summary_rationale: Eli Lilly and Company exhibits exceptional structural compounding characteristics driven by its dual-incretin (GIP/GLP-1) franchise Mounjaro and Zepbound, which reached $36.5 billion combined in FY2025 (56% of $65,179M total revenue) and exceeded $16 billion in Q3 2026 alone alongside an FDA-approved oral small-molecule GLP-1 (Foundayo/orforglipron) and late-stage triple agonist (retatrutide). Audited FY2025 operating margin expanded to 40.35% ($26,302M) with 83.04% gross margin and $16,813M operating cash flow, funding a $7,841M annual PPE capex buildout (part of >$50B cumulative U.S. manufacturing commitments) while still generating $8,972M in free cash flow and 31.6% ROIC. Key operational risks to monitor in subsequent valuation and synthesis stages include double-digit realized net price erosion (-15% YoY in Q3 2026) from payer rebates and government access agreements, intensifying oral and next-generation competition from Novo Nordisk and Amgen, persistent compounding leakage, high product concentration (56%+ in tirzepatide), and $42.5B in gross debt financing the multi-year supply chain expansion.
